blocks.text: Transferring ownership of slots, and the keys inside them, from a source master to a target master while both serve live traffic.

items: During migration the source serves keys it still holds
For keys already moved it answers `-ASK`
Clients keep working the whole time

blocks.title: MIGRATE Is Atomic Per Batch
blocks.text: DUMP-serialize, send, RESTORE on target, DELETE on source. The key exists on exactly one node at every instant — never both, never neither.

blocks.title: But It Blocks
blocks.text: MIGRATE stalls both nodes for the batch duration. One 2 GB list freezes the server. Keep batch sizes small.

items: A new node starts with zero slots and serves nothing
Deleting a node that still owns slots breaks the cluster
`--cluster-use-empty-masters` includes fresh nodes in a rebalance

blocks.title: Stuck Slot
items: Symptom: slot left MIGRATING/IMPORTING after a crash
`--cluster check` detects the open slot
`--cluster fix` clears the flag or completes the move

blocks.q: What does a reshard actually cost?

blocks.title: Rule
blocks.text: Never reshard during a failover or with any node in a fail state. Finish one topology change before you begin the next.

items: Nodes gossip on client port + 10000
Binary protocol, separate from the client port
Firewall both ports or the cluster never forms
PFAIL: no PING answer within `cluster-node-timeout`
FAIL: a majority of masters independently report PFAIL
Only masters vote — replicas gossip but do not count
An eligible replica requests votes from the masters
A majority must grant them before promotion
Disconnected too long? Ineligible
Cutoff is `cluster-node-timeout * cluster-replica-validity-factor`

blocks.title: Rank Ordering
blocks.text: The replica with the most up-to-date replication offset waits the shortest delay before campaigning, so the freshest data usually wins the election.

items: Monotonically increasing number per configuration
Highest epoch wins conflicting claims to the same slots
Old master returns, sees a higher epoch on its slots
It reconfigures itself as a replica of the winner

lines: # serve the covered slots when one

blocks.title: Manual Failover
items: `CLUSTER FAILOVER` — planned, no data loss
`FORCE` — skips the master handshake
`TAKEOVER` — skips the vote entirely, dangerous

caption.text: Part 3 of REDIS CLUSTER & SENTINEL. 16384. Not 65536, not a consistent-hashing ring — because the slot bitmap rides inside every gossip heartbeat, and 2 KB per packet beats 8 KB. That single design choice explains MOVED, ASK, CROSSSLOT, and why a hash tag of `{prod}` will haunt you forever. Ten pages on how Redis Cluster really shards, reshards and fails over, plus where Sentinel fits and where it does not.
